proofs.proof_tex:
Because \(Y_u(a,e')\) is constant in \(e'\in\mathcal E\), the definition of \(\tau_u(e)\) gives the ordinary individual treatment effect, independent of the exposure label.  Write
\[
 \tau_{(1)}(e)\leq\cdots\leq\tau_{(N)}(e)
\]
for the ordered coordinates.  Fix \(0\leq r<N\).  Since \(|U|=N\),
\[
 \sum_{u\in U}\mathbf 1\{Y_u(1,e)-Y_u(0,e)>c\}\leq r
\]
holds if and only if at least \(N-r\) coordinates of \(\tau(e)\) are at most \(c\).  By the definition of the \((N-r)\)-th order statistic, the latter condition is equivalent to
\[
 \tau_{(N-r)}(e)\leq c.
\]
This also verifies the boundary convention: a coordinate equal to \(c\) is not counted by the strict inequality.  If \(r=N\), the sum of the \(N\) indicators is always at most \(N\), so the null is vacuous.

We next verify the certificate for the partition kernel.  Let \(\mathcal G\) be the stated finite partition of \(\Omega\), and, for each \(x\in\Omega\), define
\[
 K(x,B)=\frac{\pi(B\cap G_x)}{\pi(G_x)}.
\]
Every cell is nonempty.  By \(\texttt{ass:positive-finite-design}\), \(\pi(z)>0\) for every \(z\in\Omega\); hence \(\pi(H)>0\) for every cell \(H\in\mathcal G\), and the displayed quotient is well defined.  Nonnegativity is immediate, and
\[
 \sum_{y\in\Omega}K(x,y)
 =\frac{\pi(G_x)}{\pi(G_x)}=1,
\]
so \(K\) is row-stochastic, as required by \(\texttt{ass:row-stochastic}\).

Fix a nonempty \(A\subseteq\Omega\) and an arbitrary \(\sigma\in\operatorname{Ord}(A)\).  For every cell \(H\in\mathcal G\) such that \(A\cap H\neq\varnothing\), let \(j_H\) be the position in \(\sigma\) of the last element of \(A\cap H\).  Since each prefix \(P_j(\sigma)\) is contained in \(A\), while every element of \(A\cap H\) has appeared by time \(j_H\),
\[
 P_{j_H}(\sigma)\cap H=A\cap H.
\]
Moreover, \(\sigma_{j_H}\in H\), so \(G_{\sigma_{j_H}}=H\), and therefore
\[
 K\bigl(\sigma_{j_H},P_{j_H}(\sigma)\bigr)
 =\frac{\pi(A\cap H)}{\pi(H)}.
\]
Consequently,
\[
 \max_{1\leq j\leq |A|}K\bigl(\sigma_j,P_j(\sigma)\bigr)
 \geq
 \max_{H\in\mathcal G}\frac{\pi(A\cap H)}{\pi(H)}
 \geq
 \sum_{H\in\mathcal G}\pi(H)
       \frac{\pi(A\cap H)}{\pi(H)}
 =\sum_{H\in\mathcal G}\pi(A\cap H)
 =\pi(A).
\]
Here the ratio for a cell disjoint from \(A\) is zero; the second inequality follows because the nonnegative weights \(\{\pi(H):H\in\mathcal G\}\) sum to one, and the final equality uses that the cells partition \(\Omega\).  Since \(\sigma\) was arbitrary, \(\texttt{def:subset-degeneracy}\) yields
\[
 d_K(A)=\min_{\sigma\in\operatorname{Ord}(A)}
       \max_{1\leq j\leq |A|}K\bigl(\sigma_j,P_j(\sigma)\bigr)
 \geq\pi(A).
\]
This applies both to the one-cell exchangeable complete-randomization construction and to the partition induced by the product of exchangeable fixed-treatment-count within-stratum randomizations.

By \(\texttt{thm:universal-validity-iff}\), the last display makes the partition kernel universally valid.  Under \(\texttt{ass:fixed-potential-outcomes}\), \(Y\) is fixed and \(X\sim\pi\) is the only random object.  The exposure restriction, legal-comparison imputability, fixed weak-order rule, and pre-outcome choice of \((L,K)\) are exactly \(\texttt{ass:fixed-peer-exposure}\), \(\texttt{ass:statistic-imputability}\), \(\texttt{ass:fixed-rank-statistic}\), and \(\texttt{ass:outcome-free-kernel}\), respectively.  Thus \(\texttt{thm:composite-null-validity}\), with respectively \(T=T_{\mathrm C}\) and \(T=T_{\mathrm S}\), gives for every \(\alpha\in[0,1]\)
\[
 Y\in\Theta_{r,c}(X,Y^{\mathrm{obs}})
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 \Pr_{X\sim\pi}\!\left\{p^{\mathrm{wc}}_{r,c}(X)\leq\alpha\right\}
 \leq\alpha.
\]
This is finite-sample validity of the frozen schedule-supremum test for its own score map.  Independently, the comparator-specific individual and simultaneous confidence conclusions follow directly from the cited leaves \(\texttt{lem:caughey-quantile-specialization}\) and \(\texttt{lem:suli-knapsack-specialization}\).  Those results concern their respective comparator constructions and do not identify either construction with \(\texttt{def:schedule-score}\).

It remains to establish the asserted obstruction to such an identification.  Take \(N=2\), let \(x_i\) be the assignment treating unit \(i\) and not the other unit, and set
\[
 \Omega=\{x_1,x_2\},\qquad
 \pi(x_1)=\pi(x_2)=\frac12,
 \qquad K(x_i,x_j)=\frac12\quad(1\leq i,j\leq2).
\]
For a singleton \(A=\{x_i\}\), \(\texttt{def:subset-degeneracy}\) gives \(d_K(A)=1/2=\pi(A)\).  For \(A=\Omega\), either ordering has prefix masses \(1/2\) and \(1\), so \(d_K(\Omega)=1=\pi(\Omega)\).  Hence this smallest complete-randomization kernel meets the universal-validity certificate exactly.

Choose \(\phi(j)=j\), set \(T=T_{\mathrm C}\), and, for every \(e'\in\mathcal E\), define the no-interference schedule
\[
 \theta_1(0,e')=1,\quad \theta_1(1,e')=3,
 \qquad
 \theta_2(0,e')=0,\quad \theta_2(1,e')=2.
\]
Suppose \(X=x_1\).  Then \(Y^{\mathrm{obs}}=(3,0)\).  Under \(x_1\), the schedule-imputed outcome vector is \((3,0)\), whose treated unit has ascending rank two.  Under \(x_2\), it is \((1,2)\), whose treated unit again has ascending rank two.  There are no ties.  Therefore \(\texttt{def:caughey-rank-score}\) and \(\texttt{def:schedule-score}\) give
\[
 s_\theta(x_1)=2=s_\theta(x_2).
\]
Using \(\texttt{def:kernel-tail-value}\) and row-stochasticity,
\[
 p_K(x_1;s_\theta)
 =\frac12\mathbf 1\{2\geq2\}
  +\frac12\mathbf 1\{2\geq2\}=1.
\]
Both schedule effects equal two, so
\[
 \sum_{u=1}^{2}\mathbf 1\{\theta_u(1,e)-\theta_u(0,e)>2\}=0.
\]
The schedule is consistent with \((x_1,Y^{\mathrm{obs}})\); hence \(\theta\in\Theta_{0,2}(x_1,Y^{\mathrm{obs}})\) by \(\texttt{def:bounded-null-schedules}\).  It follows from \(\texttt{def:worst-case-pvalue}\) that
\[
 p^{\mathrm{wc}}_{0,2}(x_1)\geq p_K(x_1;s_\theta)=1.
\]
Every kernel tail value lies in \([0,1]\) by nonnegativity and row-stochasticity, so the supremum is at most one and
\[
 p^{\mathrm{wc}}_{0,2}(x_1)=1.
\]

For the Caughey adjusted-outcome upper-tail construction at the boundary \(c=2\), instead hold fixed across reallocations
\[
 a=Y^{\mathrm{obs}}-2\bigl(Z_1(x_1),Z_2(x_1)\bigr)=(1,0).
\]
The treated unit has ascending rank two under \(x_1\) and rank one under \(x_2\).  Thus
\[
 T_{\mathrm C}(x_1,a)=2,
 \qquad T_{\mathrm C}(x_2,a)=1,
\]
and its upper-tail randomization value at \(x_1\) is
\[
 \sum_{j=1}^{2}\pi(x_j)
 \mathbf 1\!\left\{T_{\mathrm C}(x_j,a)\geq T_{\mathrm C}(x_1,a)\right\}
 =\frac12.
\]
This differs from the frozen worst-case value one.  Finally, take \(S=1\), \(\mathcal U=\{U\}\), and \(\phi_1=\phi\).  By \(\texttt{def:suli-stratified-rank-score}\), the within-stratum ranks then equal the full-sample ranks and \(T_{\mathrm S}=T_{\mathrm C}\); the same \(1\)-versus-\(1/2\) discrepancy follows.  The witness proves that neither exact equality with the Caughey adjusted-outcome test nor exact reuse of the Su--Li knapsack reduction follows from the frozen score construction, while the order-statistic equivalence and finite-sample validity established above remain intact.
